title: By the horses that run until they pant.
subtitle: An oath by full effort
then: Arabia was full of tribal raids at dawn, and every listener knew the sound of horses. Ibn Kathir says Allah swears by horses {idea}galloping in His path{/idea}, running until you hear them pant. The oath leads to one point: {trap}man is ungrateful to his Lord{/trap}.
now: Think of something that gives everything for whoever feeds it: a loyal dog at the door, a horse that runs flat out when called. Then think of how you answer {idea}the One who feeds you{/idea}. The oath is setting up that comparison.
old: An oath about horses has nothing to do with me.
new: Allah draws my eye to a creature giving its all, before asking what I give.
try: Watch any animal today for one minute and think about who provides for it, and for you.

title: Hooves on rock, striking sparks of fire.
subtitle: Running so hard the stones flash
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the striking of their hooves on the rocks{/idea}, which makes sparks of fire fly. The listeners had seen it. The oath builds speed and force, verse by verse, toward its point.
now: You know what full effort looks like. You have seen it at a deadline, a match, a wedding you organized. Sparks fly. {trap}Then prayer time comes and you trot.{/trap} The picture asks where your sparks go.
old: I give my best where it counts: work, family, my goals.
new: Full effort is a gift from Allah. I can bring some of it back to Him.
try: Give your next prayer the focus you would give an important meeting.

title: Charging at dawn, while others still sleep.
subtitle: The early morning raid
then: Raids at dawn were the dread of Arabia. Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ would wait at dawn to {idea}listen for the adhan{/idea} from a people. If he heard it, {reward}he left them alone{/reward}.
now: Dawn in your house: alarms snoozed, curtains shut, the phone the first thing you reach for. In that story {idea}the call to prayer was a shield{/idea}. Is the adhan heard from your home at dawn?
old: Dawn is just for sleeping in when I can.
new: Dawn is when a home shows whether Allah's name is called in it.
try: Tomorrow, say the words of the adhan quietly to yourself when you wake at Fajr.

title: Dust thrown up in clouds behind them.
subtitle: The trail that effort leaves
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the dust at the place of the battle{/idea}, stirred up by the horses. Each verse of the oath adds a detail the Arabs knew well: the panting, the sparks, the dawn, now {trap}the dust cloud{/trap}.
now: Everything you chase leaves a dust cloud. The late nights, the stress, the people you rushed past. Some trails you will be proud of. {trap}Some you will wish settled faster.{/trap} Look back at your week's dust.
old: I just keep moving. I do not look back at what I stir up.
new: Every chase leaves a trail. I want mine to be worth looking at.
try: Tonight, look back over today and name one thing you stirred up that you need to settle.

title: Plunging together into the very centre.
subtitle: The end of the charge
then: Ibn Abbas and others said this means {idea}into the midst of the enemy{/idea}, all together. Here the five-verse oath ends. Everything has been heading somewhere, and the next verse says what: {trap}man and his Lord{/trap}.
now: You have been reading a vivid scene, like the first minutes of a film. Now the camera turns. {idea}It turns to you.{/idea} Every oath in the Quran is a door, and this one opens onto your own heart.
old: The opening of a surah is just setting the scene.
new: The oath was building toward me. Allah wanted my full attention first.
try: Before reading the next verse, pause for a breath and ask Allah to show you yourself honestly.

title: Man counts his troubles and forgets the favours.
subtitle: What all the oaths were sworn about
then: This is what all the oaths were sworn about. A long list of early scholars said {trap}al-kanud means ungrateful{/trap}. Al-Hasan put it sharply: {idea}the kanud is the one who counts his calamities and forgets Allah's favours{/idea}.
now: Someone asks how you are. You list the traffic, the boss, the back pain, the bills. You do not mention the eyesight, the warm bed, the child who hugged you. {trap}Kanud.{/trap} Most of us are, most days.
old: I am not ungrateful. I am just honest about how hard things are.
new: If I can list my troubles faster than my blessings, the verse is describing me.
try: Write down five blessings from today before you write or say a single complaint.

title: And he is his own witness to it.
subtitle: Ingratitude shows in word and deed
then: Qatadah and Sufyan said {idea}Allah is a witness to that{/idea}. Al-Qurazi said it can also mean {trap}man is a witness against himself{/trap}: it is obvious from his statements and his deeds.
now: Scroll back through your messages from last week. Count the complaints. Count the thank-yous. {trap}Your own words are the evidence.{/trap} You do not need anyone else to testify.
old: Deep down I am grateful, even if I do not say it.
new: My words and actions already show what I am. I can change what they show.
try: Send one message today that only says thank you, to Allah in dua or to a person who helped you.

title: His love of wealth is fierce.
subtitle: Where the ungrateful heart is tied
then: Ibn Kathir says khayr here means wealth. One view is {trap}he is severe in his love of it{/trap}. The other is {trap}he is covetous and stingy because of it{/trap}. He says both views are correct.
now: Payday comes and the number in your banking app decides your mood for the week. A friend asks for a small loan and you feel your chest tighten. {idea}The verse names the grip.{/idea} Naming it is the first step to loosening it.
old: Wanting more money is just being responsible.
new: Money is a favour from Allah. When I love it fiercely, I grip what I should thank Him for.
try: Give away a small amount today, enough that you feel it, and notice your grip loosen.

title: Does he not know the graves will be emptied?
subtitle: The question that ends the race
then: Ibn Kathir says here Allah {idea}encourages turning away from worldly things and striving for the Hereafter{/idea}. The question means the dead in the graves {trap}will be brought out{/trap}. Maududi notes the surah shows how man behaves when he forgets this.
now: You plan five years ahead: the promotion, the house, the savings target. Rarely do you plan for the day {idea}the grave gives you back{/idea}. The question is gentle: do you not know? You do. You just do not think about it.
old: I will think about death when I am older.
new: The race for wealth ends at a grave that will open. I plan for that finish line too.
try: Add one thing to your plans this year that is only for the Hereafter.

title: What hides in the heart will be brought out.
subtitle: Intentions, not just actions, exposed
then: Ibn Abbas and others said {idea}what was in their souls will be exposed and made apparent{/idea}. Maududi says the surah warns that not only visible deeds but {trap}even the secrets of the heart{/trap} will be examined.
now: You donated, but partly to be seen. You visited, but mostly out of duty. You smiled, but with a grudge. {idea}Allah will bring out the why behind the what.{/idea} That also means the good you hid will come out.
old: As long as I do the right thing, my reasons are my business.
new: My reasons will come out. I can clean them now, while only Allah sees them.
try: Before one good deed today, stop and quietly make the intention: for Allah.

title: That Day, their Lord knows them completely.
subtitle: Full knowledge, full justice
then: Ibn Kathir says He {idea}knows all that they used to do{/idea} and will compensate them with what they deserve. {reward}He does not do even the slightest injustice.{/reward}
now: Nobody saw how hard you tried with your sick parent. Nobody knew the anger you swallowed at work. People misjudge you every week. {reward}Your Lord knows you completely.{/reward} That is a warning, and a great comfort.
old: Nobody really understands what I go through.
new: My Lord knows me fully, and He will never wrong me by even a speck.
try: Tell Allah in dua tonight about one struggle nobody else knows about.
